sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Reform UK investigates officials' violent threats and discriminatory views
cards.content: Reform UK is in trouble after an undercover investigation caught party officials and candidates making violent threats and expressing racist and sexist views. The party says it's investigating and has already suspended some people. Three councillors have quit the party so far. Party leader Nigel Farage has postponed a big announcement to deal with the fallout from the investigation which is expected to get worse with more revelations coming out.

cards.title: US Military Plans Strikes Against Iranian Energy, Nuclear Sites
cards.content: The US military has developed new strike plans against Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites which include the use of the "Mother of All Bombs" (MOAB) if President Trump gives the order. The MOAB is the largest non-nuclear bomb in the US arsenal and its use would mark a notable escalation. The plans also include targeting Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites which could have devastating effects on the area.

cards.title: Treasury Staff to Face Accountability for Woman's Suicide
cards.content: The parents of a woman who killed herself after a disciplinary meeting at the Treasury are demanding that anyone who contributed to her death be held accountable. The Treasury had previously acknowledged its role in her death and committed to making changes to prevent similar incidents. The parents David and Anne Moffat want to know that staff who handled their daughter's disciplinary meeting have been held accountable. They are meeting with the Treasury's permanent secretary to ask questions and seek assurances that lessons will be learned to prevent another tragedy.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Tortoises Surpass Human Population on Seychelles Atoll
cards.content: Giant tortoises on a Seychelles atoll have made a remarkable recovery with nearly 183000 animals now outnumbering the country's people. This is the highest estimate yet reflecting conservation efforts and a better way of counting the animals. The tortoises were once pushed to the brink but decades of protection and monitoring have helped their population grow. The new findings highlight Aldabra Atoll as one of the Indian Ocean's outstanding conservation successes.

cards.title: Bank of America Hires Thousands to Fix Decades-Old Software Flaws
cards.content: Bank of America is working to fix software vulnerabilities by hiring thousands of employees and external contractors. This is because advanced artificial intelligence models like Mythos can find and exploit decades-old software flaws. The bank's CEO Brian Moynihan said they rushed to fix these issues and have spent a couple hundred million dollars so far.

cards.title: £25 Billion Data Centre and Solar Farm Planned for Norfolk
cards.content: A big new data centre and one of the UK's largest solar farms are being planned near King's Lynn in Norfolk. The data centre will need a lot of power up to 1 gigawatt while the solar farm will generate up to 1.3 gigawatts. The project could bring in £25 billion of investment and create thousands of jobs. The solar farm will also have battery storage and use a special cooling system that recirculates liquid. The plans are being kept simple for now but there will be a consultation and the government will have the final say on whether the project goes ahead.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Kenya Reports Second Ebola Case, 39-Year-Old Man in Quarantine
cards.content: Kenya has confirmed a second case of Ebola just 10 days after a businessman died of the virus. This new patient a 39-year-old man is a close relative of the first case and was already in quarantine when he fell ill. He's recovering because he was detected early and that's limited the chance of him passing the virus on to others. There's no evidence the virus has spread to the wider community and Kenya remains open to travel and trade.

cards.title: Kenya Confirms Second Ebola Case, 39-Year-Old Man in Quarantine
cards.content: Kenya has confirmed a second case of Ebola 10 days after a businessman died of the virus. The new patient is a 39-year-old man who is a close relative of the first case and was already in quarantine when he fell ill. He was in quarantine because he was a contact of the first case and detecting his illness early improved his chances of recovery.

cards.title: Boy Kibble Diet Gains Popularity for High-Protein Convenience
cards.content:
Here is a summary of the news article in one natural paragraph

Boy kibble is a way of eating that has become popular on social media where people strip meals back to basics to get high protein and convenience. It's a batch-cooked meal typically made with rice and ground meat with some people adding avocado for healthy fat. The diet has been popular among men especially those looking to increase their fitness as it provides a reliable way to meet protein goals. However experts warn that the diet can be imbalanced with too much protein and not enough vegetables and recommend adding some variety to the meals.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Heavy Rain and Thunderstorms Hit Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, and Chandigarh
cards.content: Delhi Haryana Punjab and Chandigarh are under orange alert for heavy rainfall thunderstorms hailstorms and strong winds reaching 50 kmph. Delhi-NCR could receive up to 204.4 mm of rain causing concerns over waterlogging traffic congestion lightning strikes and travel disruptions. The weather department warns of severe weather conditions including lightning strong winds and substantial rainfall which could disrupt road traffic agricultural activities and cause waterlogging.

cards.title: Zimbabwe sets up $500 million reserve for drought preparation
cards.content: Zimbabwe is preparing for a possible drought by setting up a $500 million cash and grain reserve. This move comes after the country's Cabinet approved a plan to ensure food security and protect livelihoods.

cards.title: Indonesia Reports 1.06 Million Wildfire Hotspots, 896,000 Hectares Burned
cards.content: As of October 14 Indonesia has detected over 1.06 million wildfire hotspots surpassing the 885000 recorded in 2019. So far nearly 896000 hectares of land have burned mostly due to dry conditions and slash-and-burn practices. The situation is made worse by the ongoing Super El Niño which could make the fires harder to control and increase the risk of new outbreaks. Smoke from the fires has already spread to neighboring Malaysia and Singapore affecting air quality and public health.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: La Bola Negra Nominated for Best Picture Academy Awards
cards.content: A film called La Bola Negra is a contender for the Academy Awards' best picture prize. The movie tells three stories of gay men across a century in Spain exploring themes of love repression and self-punishment. The film has received critical acclaim and is a commercial hit in Spain. It's known for its beautiful visuals complex storyline and courage in showing sexual desire. The directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi have been praised for their work and the film's cast including Álvaro Lafuente Calvo and Carlos González have also received recognition.

cards.title: Lena Dunham Revives Girls for Limited Run with Original Cast
cards.content: Lena Dunham the creator of the popular TV show Girls announced that the show will return for a limited run after a 10-year hiatus. The revival will feature five episodes and reunite the original cast including Allison Williams Jemima Kirke Zosia Mamet and Andrew Rannells. Dunham said she's been missing the characters and that they started talking to her again around her 40th birthday. The show will explore what's happened to the characters since they were in their 20s.

cards.title: Rob Brydon Voices New Animated "The Baddies" Adaptation
cards.content: Welsh actor Rob Brydon is voicing a new animated adaptation of the popular children's book "The Baddies" over the Christmas period. The story follows a troll a ghost and a witch as they try to steal a blue spotty hanky from a brave little girl. Brydon will be joined by Gavin and Stacey co-stars Sheridan Smith and Alison Steadman as well as Hammed Animashaun Robyn Cara and Francesca Mills. The half-hour special celebrates kindness and standing up to bullies and features beautiful animation.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: US Inflation Hits 3.7% Amid Petrol Price Spike
cards.content: US inflation rose to 3.7% in the year to September higher than expected. The main cause was a big jump in petrol prices which increased by 34.2% over 12 months. This was due to disruptions to Middle East energy supplies caused by the US-Israel conflict with Iran. The cost-of-living pressures are a key issue in the upcoming midterm elections.

cards.title: Tennessee Teacher's Struggle Highlights Widespread US Cost of Living Crisis
cards.content: Kathryn Vaughn a 46-year-old art teacher in Tennessee is struggling to make ends meet due to rising costs of living. She works three jobs to support her family of four including her young son and has resorted to selling items online and writing obituaries to make extra money. Vaughn is not alone as millions of Americans are facing increased expenses for daily necessities like food gas and housing.

cards.title: UK Economy Shows Resilience with 0.1% Growth in August Despite Expectations
cards.content: The UK economy grew by 0.1% in August beating expectations of a slight contraction. Chancellor John Healey called this a sign of resilience and said it's a result of the government's fiscal discipline. The economy grew by 0.7% over the three months to August with production increasing but the services industry and construction sector were flat or contracting. The growth was driven by an increase in computer programming and the development of AI infrastructure.
